title: IPC API: Board.update_items() intermittently crashes KiCad with null dereference in _eeschema.dll (Windows, 10.0.4, schematic editor open, no interactive edit in session)
description:
# Description

Calling `Board.update_items()` from the IPC API (kicad-python / kipy 0.7.1) can **crash the whole KiCad process**. The call does not need to modify anything: echoing back a single unmodified footprint is enough. Read-only API calls (ping, get_version, get_open_documents, get_board, get_footprints, reading pads/fields) all work fine in the same session immediately before the crash.

The crash is an access violation in `_eeschema.dll` (null `this` pointer, `mov rcx, [rax+1C8h]` with `rax=0`), on the main thread, inside a tool-framework coroutine (bottom stack frame is boost::context `make_fcontext`). A *board* write via the API appears to trigger a schematic-side handler whose target object has not been created yet.

## Conditions observed (2026-07-17..18, many runs)

- The schematic editor being **open** appears to be a necessary condition: with only pcbnew open (schematic never opened in the session), the crash never occurred (3/3 clean runs). With both editors open and no interactive edit, the write crashed repeatedly.
- Performing an interactive edit + save in pcbnew (move a footprint, Ctrl+S) before the first API write reliably prevents the crash for the rest of the session. (Not yet isolated whether the edit alone or the save alone is sufficient.)
- Reproducibility is intermittent and appears related to system warm-up state: after several crash/restart cycles on a warmed-up system the crash stopped reproducing entirely, but **a Windows reboot made it reproducible again** on the first KiCad session. This smells like an initialization race whose window depends on cold vs. warm OS caches.
- At some point crash/no-crash alternated between consecutive KiCad sessions (crashing session -> next session immune -> clean exit -> next session crashes again). A diff of the settings profile between the "immune" and "vulnerable" states showed no meaningful difference (only `last_update_check_time` and window geometry noise in `kicad.json`), so the alternation is presumably also a warm-up/timing artifact rather than persistent state.
- The vulnerable state is not fixed by waiting alone in at least some cases: one captured crash dump shows process uptime of 7h25m before the fatal first API write of that session.
- No WER "Application Error" event is logged and no fresh WER dump is produced (exception is presumably captured in-process); the process silently disappears ~0.5 s after the request (the IPC pipe drops, the client then gets `ConnectionError: Error receiving reply from KiCad: Timed out`).

# Steps to reproduce

Best chance to reproduce: freshly rebooted Windows, first KiCad session.

1. Start KiCad, open a project, open **both** the schematic and the PCB. Do **not** edit or save anything.
2. Run the following against the running instance (`pip install kicad-python==0.7.1`):

```python
from kipy import KiCad

k = KiCad()
board = k.get_board()
fp = board.get_footprints()[0]
board.update_items([fp])   # no-op echo of an unmodified footprint
```

3. KiCad terminates within ~0.5 s.

On 2026-07-17 this reproduced on every attempt across multiple KiCad restarts (88-footprint 4-layer board, Cyclone 10 FPGA project); it also matches crashes captured on 2026-07-04 and 2026-07-09 during normal use of an IPC-based placement tool. After system warm-up it stops reproducing.

# WinDbg analysis of the attached crash dump (WER LocalDumps, 2026-07-09)

```
ExceptionCode: c0000005 (Access violation), reading 0x00000000000001c8
KEY_VALUES: AV.Dereference = NullClassPtr, AV.Fault = Read
FAILURE_BUCKET_ID: NULL_CLASS_PTR_READ_c0000005__eeschema.dll!Unknown

rax=0000000000000000  rip=00007ffa128cbb5a (_eeschema.dll+0x7ABB5A)
_eeschema+0x7ABB5A: mov rcx, qword ptr [rax+1C8h]

Stack (module-relative offsets; no public PDBs available to me):
  _eeschema+0x7ABB5A   <- fault, null this
  _eeschema+0x8CA19B
  _eeschema+0x99D867
  _eeschema+0xA56E8C
  _eeschema+0x918B61
  _eeschema!make_fcontext+0x5A   <- boost::context, tool-framework coroutine entry
```

Module base was 0x7FFA12120000 (offsets above are module-relative so they can be symbolized against the 10.0.4 Windows build). Full `.dmp` attached, together with a timestamped client-side log of a crashing session from 2026-07-17 showing 8 successful read stages followed by the fatal no-op `update_items`.

API server: 10.0.1 (10.0.1-0-g2db9e5a72b), client kicad-python (kipy) 0.7.1, Python 3.12.10.

Possibly related: #20206 (update_items crash on v9, but that one required actual data changes; this one crashes on a no-op echo).
